sections.h2: Who records deeds in Wyoming County
sections.html:
One elected officeholder serves as both Register of Wills and Recorder of Deeds, working from the courthouse in the county seat, Tunkhannock. Every deed and mortgage on a county parcel is filed there, alongside estate paperwork.

Counter service runs weekdays from 8:30 to 4:00, and the last filing is taken at 3:45 in the afternoon. Call (570) 996-2361 with questions. Only cash and checks are accepted. Electronic recording, electronic filing and e-signatures are all unavailable, so whoever closes your sale must hand-deliver or mail the paper deed bearing original signatures.

Land records here start in 1842, when the county was created out of Luzerne County. Papers filed before February 2007 are cited by book and page, while later ones use an instrument number. Either reference will bring up the deed by which you took title through the online deed search on the county website.

Filing a deed costs $64.75 at base on the schedule dated December 1, 2025. That amount covers four pages and four names. A fifth page and beyond adds $2.00 apiece, and extra names beyond four add $0.50 apiece.

A flat $20 lien search fee and a $30 base fee for maps took effect November 1, 2026, and the full schedule was revised then, so request the current sheet before writing your check.

Wyoming County base recording fees

Deed$64.75
Mortgage$64.75

Pay the exact sum. Anything over by $5.00 or less stays with the county, a larger overpayment gets the document sent back, and there are no refunds. Checks go to the order of the Wyoming County Recorder of Deeds.

Expect 2 percent in total: one point goes to the state and one point to local government. The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue sets the 1 percent state piece, and recorders gather it along with the local tax.

No deed is accepted until the tax is in hand. A single check can cover a taxable transaction, with no separate check for the tax.

Gifts inside the family can be exempt. The recorder's FAQ names husband and wife, parent and child, grandparent and grandchild, and siblings, and it suggests talking to an attorney before counting on the exemption. Whenever an exemption is claimed, or the price paid differs from the one printed on the deed, a Statement of Value form must go in with two copies.

sections.h2: What a deed must look like
sections.html:
Pages that break the formatting or notary rules come back unrecorded, so have the deed checked before it leaves your hands. The requirements include:

  • Ink signatures with a notary acknowledgment that is not dated before the deed. Photocopies are refused.
  • Font size 9 or bigger, half an inch of clear space at the top of each page, black and white only, and no staples.
  • The property's municipality, county and state written out, and a price in words that agrees with the price in figures.
  • A signed certification of address attached to each deed and mortgage.
  • A stamped return envelope, addressed to you and big enough for the original.

No parcel or PIN number is needed on a Wyoming County deed. Two cases add paperwork. A parcel spanning several municipalities calls for a Statement of Value giving the whole-number share of local tax for each. A taxable sale in Windham Township calls for one too, so the school district is correct.

To fix an earlier deed, a corrective or confirmatory deed has to carry a Statement of Value, say why it is being corrected, and attach the old deed. The recorder does not vouch for what a document says. Staff confirm only that the rules are met and the fees and taxes are paid.

sections.h2: Getting the deed back and searching records
sections.html:
A recorded original typically returns by mail about a week later, workload permitting, since staff proof, scan, index and verify each one. The office cannot add, drop or alter names on a recorded deed. Only a newly drafted deed can do that.

The courthouse computers and the online deed search both let you look through the records. Certified copies run $5.00 through eight pages and $0.50 for each page beyond. Staff look up documents by full name only. To trace an owner from a parcel number or street address, turn to the county GIS site or phone the assessment office.

Liens are split between offices. This one records mortgages and UCC filings. Other liens and judgments sit with the Prothonotary, the Clerk of Courts or Orphans' Court, so a seller worried about judgments needs to search those too.

sections.h2: Wyoming County housing at a glance
sections.html: Rural Wyoming County sits in the northeastern corner of the state with about 25,790 people and 12,989 housing units. Owners live in 77.9 percent of homes, the median owner-occupied value is $215,400 and typical gross rent is $943 a month. Many owners are older, 24.3 percent of residents being 65 or over, so houses often pass through estates. The Register of Wills half of this same office handles letters and the inheritance tax forms for them. Winters are cold, which is why inspectors look hard at roofs, plumbing and heating.

sections.h2: Steps for a Wyoming County sale
sections.html:
Because nothing can be filed electronically, plan the deed's trip to Tunkhannock. Your title company or attorney will mail it or carry it to the courthouse before 3:45 p.m. with the exact check, the Statement of Value if one is needed, the certification of address and a stamped return envelope.

Ask them to read the deed against the requirements list first. A photocopied signature, a notary date that falls before the deed date, or a price in words that disagrees with the figures all lead to a rejected filing and a lost week. A cash sale skips the lender paperwork, but the same office, the same fees and the same transfer tax apply.

Call (570) 996-2361 if you are unsure about a form or a fee total. Ask when the original is likely to come back, and watch the mail for it, since the return envelope you supplied is the only way it reaches you. Once it is recorded, keep that original with your closing papers.

faqs.q: Does Wyoming County accept e-recording for deeds?
faqs.a: No. The Recorder of Deeds does not accept e-recording, e-filing or e-signatures. Deliver the paper deed in person or by mail, with original notary signatures and a self-addressed stamped return envelope.

faqs.q: What is the realty transfer tax rate in Wyoming County?
faqs.a: It is 2 percent of the price, split 1 percent state and 1 percent local. The deed is not accepted until the tax is paid, and the office takes one check for one taxable transaction.

faqs.q: Do I need a parcel number to record my deed in Wyoming County?
faqs.a: No. The recorder does not require or certify PIN numbers. It does require the municipality, county and state on the document, and a Statement of Value when land lies in several municipalities or in Windham Township.

faqs.q: How much does the Wyoming County recorder charge for a mortgage satisfaction?
faqs.a: A satisfaction piece is $61.75, which covers four pages and four names. A mortgage release or assignment is $59.75. Lenders usually file the satisfaction, and the recorder cannot do it for you.

faqs.q: Where do I find who owns a property in Wyoming County?
faqs.a: Use the county GIS website or call the assessment office, which can look up ownership by parcel number or address. The recorder can only search by full name, and the online deed search shows recorded documents back to 1842.
